idea.idea: RBI Stop Switch Protocol for Digital Payment Fraud Protection in Small Businesses
idea.angle: How small merchants can leverage RBI's proposed account-wide Stop Switch to immediately halt unauthorized UPI/netbanking drains during scams.
idea.audience_problem: Small business owners worry about shop account UPI phishing scams draining business funds with no instant kill-switch.

hooks: RBI's upcoming 2027 plan to kill UPI fraud.
Stop your shop account from draining during a scam.
New RBI rules to protect your business bank account.
piece.hook_reason: It clearly frames the content as a regulatory update for 2027, avoiding the false promise of an immediate fix while highlighting the specific benefit (fraud prevention).

slides.title: RBI's upcoming 2027 plan to kill UPI fraud.
slides.subtitle: How the new account-wide Stop Switch will protect business funds from scams.

slides.title: What is the Stop Switch?
slides.body: The RBI has proposed a new feature that lets account holders instantly disable all outgoing debits, new UPI registrations, and payment mandates to stop unauthorized drains during a fraud event.

slides.title: What the Stop Switch affects
slides.body: The switch is designed to isolate your account during a security emergency.

slides.title: Proposed protection features
items: Trusted Person Mechanism for high-value transfers
Granular controls for individual payment channels
Default disable on new digital channels

slides.title: The official proposal
slides.quote: Banks will have to provide a Stop Switch that allows customers to immediately disable all outgoing debits, new payment mandates and new UPI app registrations.
slides.attribution: Reserve Bank of India Draft Directions 2026

slides.title: Key takeaways for owners
items: Draft rules invite feedback until Dec 14, 2026
Switch will be available via app, ATM, and IVR
Banks must verify trusted person eligibility

piece.caption: RBI is planning a major shift in how small businesses handle digital payment security. By 2027, banks will be required to provide a 'Stop Switch' to instantly freeze outgoing debits, giving you a way to pause your account if you suspect a scam. This is a preventive step that complements existing liability protections. While we wait for these to roll out, review your current bank app settings for transaction limits and channel disabling options. Does your current bank app allow you to disable UPI or netbanking instantly if you lose your phone? RBI Proposes ‘Stop Switch’ To Block Digital Payment Frauds --> tag --> Skip to content RBI Proposes ‘Stop Switch’ To Block Digital Payment Frauds --> SHARE Share on Facebook
SUMMARY The RBI has proposed measures like an account-wide ‘Stop Switch’, a ‘Trusted Person Mechanism’, and granular customer controls over digital payments
After directives to limit customers’ liability in digital frauds, these new protections will help customers take a proactive and preventive approach
The ‘Stop Switch’ would disable outgoing debits while the Trusted Person Mechanism would serve as an additional authentication layer for high-value transfers
Added to Saved Stories in Login VIEW SAVED STORIES
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed a set of safeguards against electronic payment frauds, including an account-wide ‘Stop Switch’ and a ‘Trusted Person Mechanism’ (TPM) for high-value transactions.
The central bank has invited feedback on the draft directions by December 14, 2026, with the proposed rules set to come into effect from July 1, 2027.
Under the Draft Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026, banks will have to provide a ‘Stop Switch’ that allows customers to immediately disable all outgoing debits, new payment mandates and new UPI app registrations.
The switch will not block incoming credits or existing standing instructions. Customers will be able to activate, modify or deactivate it through bank branches, ATMs, mobile apps, internet banking and interactive voice response (IVR) services.
Banks will also have to ensure that re-enabling digital payment channels or deactivating the Stop Switch requires at least the same level of authentication as its activation.
The RBI has also proposed a voluntary Trusted Person Mechanism (TPM) for high-value transfers. Under this facility, account holders can nominate an adult as an additional authentication layer for transactions above a specified threshold.
The nominated person will have to approve such transactions within a one-hour window. However, the trusted person will not have any legal authority over the account or access to its details.
Banks will be responsible for verifying the identity and eligibility of nominated individuals. Any activation or modification of the TPM will also be subject to a 24-hour cooling-off period.
The RBI had first floated a similar proposal in June this year, suggesting an additional authentication layer for digital transactions above ₹10,000 made by citizens aged 70 and above.
Beyond these measures, banks will have to offer customers granular controls over their digital payment channels. These will include options to enable or disable individual channels, set time windows for their deactivation and establish transaction limits per transfer, per beneficiary or through aggregate daily caps.
The draft also proposes that all digital payment channels remain disabled by default during customer onboarding and be activated only with explicit consent.
Further, newly issued physical and virtual cards will be restricted by default to domestic contact-based ATM and point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Newly enabled digital payment channels will also be subject to a transfer limit determined by the bank for the first 24 hours.
Earlier this year, the central bank issued directions requiring banks to compensate eligible victims of digital payment frauds. The latest proposals take a more preventive approach, giving customers greater control over payment channels and adding authentication safeguards to help stop fraudulent transactions before they are completed.
